study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
outcome: Composite of uterotonic use after initial postpartum oxytocin
Postpartum hemorrhage (estimated blood loss >500 mL after vaginal delivery and >1000 mL after cesarean delivery)
Individual composite components and select bleeding outcomes
cohort: The study included 2404 nulliparous women with term singleton pregnancies from a primary randomized controlled trial.
finding: High-dose postpartum oxytocin was associated with significantly lower odds of the primary composite outcome and postpartum hemorrhage compared to lower oxytocin doses.
mod_finding: The effect of oxytocin dose on the primary outcome did not differ by delivery mode, with results appearing consistent for both vaginal and cesarean deliveries.
followup_time: Outcomes were measured in the immediate postpartum period.
